correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the complete-kill event fixes the nth label to be rank one in each independent coordinate permutation and leaves the relative ranks of the first \(n-1\) labels uniform. Sorting by the first coordinate converts current Pareto minima into left-to-right minima of a uniform permutation. Independent sequential relative ranks give probability generating function \(z(z+1)\cdots(z+n-2)/(n-1)!\), hence the unsigned-Stirling formula. Fixed-degree elementary-symmetric asymptotics then give \(C_{n,k}\sim n^{-3}(\log n)^{k-1}/(k-1)!\). The exact Theorem 3.9 remainder has coefficient \(1/4\) on \(C_{n,k}\) and only lower \(C_{n,j}\), which satisfy \(C_{n,j}=o(C_{n,k})\) for fixed \(j<k\). Boundaries \(n\ge2\), \(1\le k\le n-1\), and fixed-\(k\) asymptotics are explicit. Finite checks are supplementary, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating full text identifies \(C_k\) probabilistically, gives only a finite-sum formula and three special cases, and explicitly leaves the fixed-\(k\) sharp remainder rate as a conjecture. Exact searches for the paper, \(C_k\), complete kills, Stirling/cycle aliases, and the \(n^{-3}(\log n)^{k-1}\) rate found no covering indexed or published statement. The later multivariate paper treats the limiting broken-record law, not this finite-sample component. The classical Stirling law for ordinary permutation records is acknowledged as prior; the new step is the conditional-rank identification of Fill\'s \(C_k\) and its consequence for the stated conjecture.
residual_risks: The reduction is short once one recognizes the classical record-count law, so an equivalent observation could exist under the language of planar maxima, permutation records, or skyline size and remain unindexed.

The originality claim is limited to the exact complete-kill identification and its consequence for Fill's stated fixed-k conjecture; it does not claim novelty of the unsigned-Stirling law for ordinary records.

value.rationale: The exact law is structurally motivated by the complete-kill component that controls the error term in the motivating paper. It converts an opaque finite-sum family into a classical permutation statistic, supplies an all-n generating function and exact probabilities, and directly proves a named fixed-k sharp-error conjecture with its leading constant. This is not an arbitrary finite slice or table recomputation; the consequence holds for every fixed k and every finite n in the exact component.
